headline: Funding flows. Contracts canceled. GPS jamming persists.
deck: This week, the Space Force's budget grows, while GPS jamming remains a concern.

stories.head: Space Force's budget ballooned to $55.5 billion
stories.body: The House Appropriations Committee approved a hefty $55.5 billion budget for the U.S. Space Force, signaling a robust commitment to satellite communications and space resilience. This funding comes amid increasing competition in satellite technology, as the military seeks to stay ahead of global adversaries. The emphasis on satellite communications suggests a shift towards more integrated military operations in space.
stories.soWhat: It seems that the Space Force is trying to outspend its way to superiority, but budget size doesn’t always equate to effectiveness.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion as it focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness. The funding reflects a growing interest in safeguarding satellite operations, particularly as geopolitical tensions rise. With the Department of Defense's backing, True Anomaly is well-positioned to capitalize on the increasing demand for security solutions in space.
stories.soWhat: In a world where satellites are the new gold, True Anomaly's cash infusion shows that investors are betting on the need to protect that gold.

stories.head: Space Force seeks new bidders after $1.7B contract axed
stories.body: After terminating a $1.7 billion contract for satellite-control antennas, the Space Force is back in the market for fresh bids. This decision highlights the challenges of managing complex contracts in the defense sector, where expectations often clash with reality. The move indicates that the Space Force is not afraid to pivot when things go sideways, even at a significant financial cost.
stories.soWhat: This is a classic case of 'try, fail, and try again'—but with taxpayer dollars at stake, the stakes are a bit higher than usual.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on GPS jamming trends
watchlist.body: With GPS jamming in the Eastern Med returning to pre-2024 levels, stakeholders should assess how this impacts satellite operations and insurance models.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser progress
watchlist.body: Having cleared its critical design review, the next steps for Sierra Space will be closely watched as they attempt to deliver on their promises without further delays.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension implications
watchlist.body: With a $480 million extension on the TITAN program, Palantir's approach to data management in defense will be a focal point for future government contracts.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris collaboration
watchlist.body: Their tactical SDA constellation bid could set a precedent for future partnerships in defense tech, especially as competition heats up.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
